title: The SOAP envelope must be SOAP 1.1
method: raw Discover through the msmdpump listener (127.0.0.1:8090)
repro: POST a Discover in a SOAP 1.2, foreign-namespace or XMLA-default envelope: each faults. Any prefix bound to the SOAP 1.1 namespace is accepted.
notes: The prefix is irrelevant, the resolved namespace is not. A foreign element that merely shares a skeleton name (a SOAP header entry called `Header`, say) is an extension and is accepted.

title: Every element the server interprets must resolve to the XMLA namespace
method: raw Discover probes
repro: A foreign- or undeclared-prefixed `RequestType`, `Execute`, `Command`, `Statement`, `Restrictions`, `RestrictionList` or `PropertyName` faults; the same elements bound to `urn:schemas-microsoft-com:xml-analysis` are accepted, prefixed or not.
notes: Elements the server merely passes over — the engine's own `<Version>` header, engine property names in a `PropertyList` — are not namespace-checked.

title: Restrictions are a flat `<RestrictionList>` and nothing else
method: raw Discover probes
repro: Nested `<restriction>` elements, `<column>`/`<value>` pairs and raw named children directly under `<Restrictions>` all fault as schema errors.
notes: A `<Value>` child carries a restriction's value only inside the element that names it (`<PropertyName><Value>Catalog</Value></PropertyName>`); a direct `<Value>` is an unrecognised restriction name.

title: An unknown restriction name faults
method: raw Discover probes
repro: `<RestrictionList><BOGUS_NAME>x</BOGUS_NAME></RestrictionList>` answers `The restriction, BOGUS_NAME, is not recognized by the server.`
notes: The accepted name set per rowset is exactly what `DISCOVER_SCHEMA_ROWSETS` advertises. An empty value does not excuse an unknown name (a self-closing `<BOGUS_NAME/>` still faults); a known name with an empty value is ignored, not applied as an empty-string filter.

title: A repeated restriction name keeps the last value
method: raw Discover probes (match-then-no-match and the reverse)
repro: Two `HIERARCHY_UNIQUE_NAME` entries: match-then-no-match returns 0 rows, no-match-then-match returns 1 — the second wins.
notes: Not an OR. Clients that want a union must send one value or query separately.

title: A scope name that matches nothing answers an empty rowset
method: raw Discover probes
repro: `MDSCHEMA_DIMENSIONS` with `CUBE_NAME=Nope` or `CATALOG_NAME=Nope` returns zero rows — not a fault, and never another catalog's rows.
notes: Not a fault, and never another catalog's rows. Measured for `CUBE_NAME`/`CATALOG_NAME` on dimensions, and — with values that match nothing — for `DIMENSION_UNIQUE_NAME`, `MEASURE_UNIQUE_NAME`, `PROPERTY_NAME` and `MEMBER_TYPE` across the members, hierarchies, measures and properties rowsets: every one answered 0 rows.

title: Element and attribute names must be valid XML QNames
method: raw Discover probes
repro: `<1Bogus/>`, `<Bad~Name/>` and a `1foo` attribute answer `Illegal qualified name character`; `<a:b:c/>` answers `A qualified name cannot contain multiple colons`.
notes: XML references are not permitted inside names, so `<Request&Type/>` is the same fault rather than a different element.

title: DTDs are prohibited outright
method: raw Discover probes
repro: An internal-subset doctype, a SYSTEM doctype and a doctype misplaced inside the body all answer `DTD is prohibited`.
notes: No entity expansion is possible: the document is rejected before parsing proper.

title: XML-invalid control characters fault wherever they appear
method: raw Discover probes
repro: U+0001 inside a comment, a processing instruction, an attribute name or an element name answers `Illegal xml character` / `Illegal qualified name character`.
notes: A literal CR is legal but is normalised to LF by every XML parser, so a server echoing it in an attribute must write `` to round-trip.

title: Sessions are header entries, and unknown ids fault
method: raw Execute probes with and without session ids
repro: `<soap:Header><Session xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:xml-analysis" SessionId="x"/></soap:Header>` reads that id; a foreign-namespace `Session` entry is ignored and a fresh id is issued. `DROP MEMBER` with an id the server does not know answers `The 'x' session ID cannot be found.`
notes: Session ids are read from the XMLA `Session`/`EndSession` header entries only; a foreign-namespace `Session` entry is ignored and a fresh id is issued. An id the server does not know is a fault, not a new session.

title: `DISCOVER_SESSIONS` reports live server state
method: ADOMD with two simultaneous connections open
repro: With two connections held open, `DISCOVER_SESSIONS` returned 2 rows; in the same probe `DISCOVER_CONNECTIONS` returned 3, `DISCOVER_TRANSACTIONS` 0, `DISCOVER_JOBS` 1, `DISCOVER_LOCKS` 0 and `DISCOVER_MEMORYUSAGE` 135.
notes: One row per live session, one row per connection for CONNECTIONS; the counts move with server activity, so only the presence of live state is the claim.

title: Session-scoped MDX DDL (`CREATE MEMBER` / `CREATE SET`)
method: raw Execute probes with a BeginSession-issued session id
repro: BeginSession → `CREATE MEMBER [Model].[Measures].[ProbeCalc] AS 42` → `SELECT {[Measures].[ProbeCalc]} ON 0 FROM [Model]` returned **42** on the same session → `DROP MEMBER` → `EndSession`, all accepted.
notes: The member created by one request resolves in a *later* request on the same session: session-scoped DDL is real, and an adapter without session state cannot honour it (MallardCube faults such statements as unsupported).

title: MSOLAP begins a session with an empty `<Statement/>`
method: trace of a real MSOLAP connection plus raw probes
repro: `<BeginSession/>` in the header plus a self-closing `<Statement/>` in the body starts a session; empty, whitespace-only and self-closing statements all answer an empty `ExecuteResponse`.
notes: Faulting an empty statement breaks every MSOLAP connection at `E_FAIL` — the single most expensive false-positive this project has hit. `BeginSession` and empty-Execute answers are the same shape from the client's point of view.

title: MSOLAP refuses a plain-HTTP msmdpump endpoint
method: connection attempts from Excel and ADODB on the test VM
repro: `Data Source=http://host:80/OLAP/msmdpump.dll` answers `Connections to SQL Server Analysis Services through msmdpump.dll must use secure channels, for example HTTPS.`
notes: A plain-HTTP listener that forwards to the HTTPS pump (or the native endpoint) is the workaround used on the reference VM; the requirement is the client's, not the pump's.

title: A stale WinINET proxy with `<-loopback>` breaks MSOLAP but not curl
method: observed while repairing the reference VM
repro: With `ProxyEnable=1` and `ProxyServer=http=127.0.0.1:8888` plus `ProxyOverride=<-loopback>`, MSOLAP fails to connect while `curl` to the same URL succeeds.
notes: `<-loopback>` means 'do not bypass the proxy for loopback', the opposite of the usual override. WinINET apps are affected; curl reads environment variables only.

title: `HIERARCHY_ORIGIN` values
method: ADOMD rowset probes against the mirror model
repro: `MDSCHEMA_HIERARCHIES`: a user hierarchy reports 1, an attribute hierarchy 2, `[Measures]` 6.
notes: A date column's key attribute hierarchy reports **2**, not the attribute|key combination 6 — with 6, Excel writes `memberValueDatatype="5"` (a double fallback) instead of the date type 7 its level advertises.

title: Excel stores `memberValueDatatype` per attribute hierarchy
method: relay capture of the pivot cache definition plus MDSCHEMA_PROPERTIES probes
repro: Excel reads the hierarchy's `MEMBER_VALUE` `DATA_TYPE` and writes it as `memberValueDatatype` on that `cacheHierarchy`. A user hierarchy gets `time="1"` (its dimension is Time) but no `memberValueDatatype`, so its levels never offer Date Filters.
notes: The full-date level must be exposed as its own single-level attribute hierarchy with `MEMBER_VALUE` DATA_TYPE 7 for Excel to offer Date Filters; `(All)` rows carry 130, period levels int, the date level 7.

title: `MDSCHEMA_PROPERTIES` is read positionally and filtered by `PROPERTY_TYPE`
method: ADOMD restricted schema probes plus relay captures
repro: With an `AdomdRestrictionCollection`: `PROPERTY_TYPE` 1, 3 and 4 answer empty; 2 answers the 12 cell properties only when the request names no cube or hierarchy; 5 answers the hierarchy's rows.
notes: Excel reads the elements positionally against the schema — order is `LEVEL_UNIQUE_NAME, PROPERTY_TYPE, PROPERTY_NAME, PROPERTY_CAPTION, DATA_TYPE, PROPERTY_ORIGIN, PROPERTY_IS_VISIBLE`. A reordered answer made Excel read 5 as `DATA_TYPE` and stamp `memberValueDatatype="5"` on every hierarchy.

title: `DISCOVER_SCHEMA_ROWSETS` must honour the `SchemaName` restriction
method: relay capture
repro: Excel asks for one rowset's entry to learn its restrictions; the reference answers with exactly that one row.
notes: Answering with the whole list makes Excel miss e.g. `HIERARCHY_VISIBILITY` and take an older metadata path — the pivot cache then lacks fields the newer path provides.

title: `PREFERRED_QUERY_PATTERNS=3` gates whether Excel asks for `MEMBER_VALUE`
method: relay captures with the value flipped
repro: With `PREFERRED_QUERY_PATTERNS` reported as 0, Excel's trace shows only `PROPERTY_TYPE=2` cell-property requests and the pivot cache gets no `memberValueDatatype`.
notes: Tabular engines report 3; without it the date-filter path is never reached regardless of the other metadata.

title: Cellset members are read positionally
method: submission of deliberately reordered cellsets to Excel
repro: A member must carry `UName`, `Caption`, `LName`, `LNum`, `DisplayInfo` in that order, then any requested dimension properties; `CHILDREN_CARDINALITY` is emitted only when the query asks for it.
notes: Shipping `CHILDREN_CARDINALITY` unrequested shifted `PARENT_UNIQUE_NAME` by one and made Excel crash on multi-level expansion, while single-level expansion still looked fine.

title: Two row fields produce a `DrilldownMember(CrossJoin(...))` request
method: traces of the sweep corpus
repro: `SELECT NON EMPTY Hierarchize(DrilldownMember(CrossJoin({[Category].[Category].[All],[Category].[Category].[Category].AllMembers}, {([Channel].[Channel].[All])}), {...}, [Channel].[Channel])) ...` is the shape Excel sends when a second field joins the row axis.
notes: Captured from real Excel; whether Excel chooses it for every nesting/field order is not fully mapped yet — hence open rather than verified. A COM Top-5 pivot filter never reaches the server as `TopCount` at all (0 in 1,156 traced requests), which is why that gap is still unexplained.

title: `DIMENSION_TYPE` and `DEFAULT_HIERARCHY`
method: ADOMD rowset probes against the reference model
repro: `MDSCHEMA_DIMENSIONS`: a time table reports 1, `[Measures]` 2, every other dimension 3; `DEFAULT_HIERARCHY` names the user hierarchy where one exists.
notes: The reference marks its date table `dataCategory: "Time"` and reports 1 for that dimension; every other dimension reports 3. Excel's time intelligence keys off the Time dimension type.

title: Level origin, type and data type values
method: ADOMD rowset probes
repro: `MDSCHEMA_LEVELS`: `LEVEL_TYPE` is 1 for `(All)` and **0 for every other level** — tabular does not use time level types; `LEVEL_DBTYPE` is 7 for a date level, 20 int64, 130 string and 3 for `(All)`; `LEVEL_ORIGIN` is 1 for user-hierarchy levels, 2 for attribute-hierarchy levels and 6 for `[Measures]`.
notes: The level's `MEMBER_VALUE` `DATA_TYPE` is what Excel reads for `memberValueDatatype`, so these values are the input to the date-filter decision.

title: Compound member unique names name the top level, then one key per level
method: raw cellset inspection
repro: A quarter under 2024 is `[DateDim].[Calendar].[Year].&[2024].&[1]`; a month under it is `…&[1].&[1]` — the top level's name with one key segment per level beneath.
notes: Excel round-trips either form — a server naming the member's own level (`[Date].[Calendar].[Quarter].&[2024]&[1]`) is also understood — but the reference form is what an exact match emits.

title: Attribute-hierarchy axis members live in their own namespace
method: raw cellset probes plus Excel field experiments
repro: `DrilldownLevel({[DateDim].[FullDate].[All]})` returns `(All)` first, then `[DateDim].[FullDate].&[2024-01-15T00:00:00]` with `LName=[DateDim].[FullDate].[FullDate]`, `LNum=1` and `PARENT_UNIQUE_NAME=[DateDim].[FullDate].[All]`.
notes: Excel places axis members by the field's hierarchy and level numbers: rendering the dates in the *user* hierarchy's namespace (level 4) leaves the field empty, and dropping the hierarchy name from the drilldown lists the user hierarchy's years instead.

title: An applied Date Filter is an MDX subquery over the key attribute
method: relay capture of Excel against the reference model
repro: `SELECT NON EMPTY Hierarchize({DrilldownLevel({[Date].[Full Date].[All]},,,INCLUDE_CALC_MEMBERS)}) DIMENSION PROPERTIES PARENT_UNIQUE_NAME,[Date].[Full Date].[Full Date]KEY0,[Date].[Full Date].[Full Date]MEMBER_VALUE ON COLUMNS FROM (SELECT Filter([Date].[Full Date].Levels(1).AllMembers, ([Date].[Full Date].CurrentMember.MemberValue = CDate("2026-09-23"))) ON COLUMNS FROM [Sales]) WHERE ([Measures].[Revenue])`.
notes: The operator follows the menu item (`=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`); `Levels(1)` is the key attribute's single level; Excel computes period items such as Today client-side and sends a plain `CDate`. The subquery's member filter must constrain the *outer axis* — answering it as an unrelated slicer returns every date.

title: The Date Filters dialog commits only through its calendar picker
method: UI automation experiments recorded in the project skills
repro: The dialog's buttons are drawn by Office (no child HWNDs), `WM_COMMAND`/`SendMessage` do not reach it, and OK stays disabled until the date field is set — its text is not committed until the calendar picker sets it. Synthetic mouse clicks work once the dialog is the foreground window.
notes: Automating it means clicking the picker's Today button, then OK. It is the one Excel path this project drives by coordinates rather than COM.

title: An empty `<Cancel/>` header does not disturb a request
method: raw Discover probe with a Cancel header
repro: A `DISCOVER_DATASOURCES` request carrying `<soap:Header><Cancel xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:xml-analysis"/></soap:Header>` returned its normal rowset — the header names no session, so there is nothing to cancel.
notes: Cancellation itself is session-scoped: the header is meaningful with a session id, and a server that ignores it lets the work finish.
